# 8086tiny source pin

The FreeDOS proof uses 8086tiny as its 8086/PC-XT core.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Upstream | <https://github.com/adriancable/8086tiny> |

| Retrieved | 2026-09-02 |
| Licence | MIT (`license.txt` in the upstream repository) |
| Upstream CPU memory backing | `RAM_SIZE = 0x10FFF0` bytes |
| Original upstream `8086tiny.c` SHA-256 | `a5a3612fbd1e5a08e29dff5a2c69d9ef49a0c28fdd7cfdf0fe6753d0ad367ee0` |

`engine/native-dos/vendor/8086tiny/8086tiny.c` is an adapted copy, not a
verbatim upstream mirror. It retains the MIT notice and replaces host file,
keyboard, graphics, and speaker access with bounded MHS callbacks. The current
firmware build links this adapter; booting the SD-backed `DOSVM.IMG` to a real
`C:\>` prompt remains the physical acceptance test.

The native adapter explicitly resets interpreter state on every start. Its
ANSI console occupies private backing memory after the guest address map and
I/O latches, preserving the BIOS-owned B800/C000/C800 display pages. The
logical backing spans 1,185,632 bytes. Firmware now uses address-based byte
transfers and an SD page cache instead of requiring that span in PSRAM.
F000 remains a permanent writable 64 KiB segment for registers, BIOS data,
and the BIOS stack. The flat host path remains available for differential
tests; REP and disk service work yield between bounded chunks.
